definition: a behaviour I am not at peace with raises the price of whatever it is tangled with

settled:
I have temporary acceptance for a behaviour I am not permanently aligned with, and the dissonance attaches itself to the object most tangled up in it.

That object is my headset, which is also the most immersive route to the best cardio I have.

The association charges the starting rather than the doing, so the price is paid before the exercise begins at all.

It is the same shape as my food aversions. Conceptual rather than sensory, pointed at a device.

So I should not build movement on a lever that needs pushing through dissonance to start. That breaks my own affordability rule, and it is the wrong foundation for a habit meant to last.

title: What A Dissonance Costs Me To Start
